section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1970
title: Incidence of Suicidal Deaths in the States, Union Territories and Cities during 1970 The regional distribution of suicidal deaths shows marked variations from State to State as compared to the previous years and as against the All-India increase of 11.0% during 1970 over 1969. There were higher increases in the States of Andhra Pradesh (18.1%), Bihar (25.9%), Madhya Pradesh (32.4%), Maharashtra (35.3%) and West Bengal (23.6%), while Gujarat (35.1%). Rajasthan (19.8%) registered significant decreases. In the Union Territories, Delhi indicated a significant increase of 55.9%. In the Cities under study, marked decreases of 235.3% and 81.3% were noticed in Bangalore and Kanpur, while Delhi (55.6%), Bombay (39.8%) and Madras (151.7%) showed marked increases during 1970 over the previous year. Wherever marked increases have been noticed over the previous year these were mainly due to 'despair over dreadful diseases' or due to 'other causes.' However, in West Bengal, a large number of suicides was due to failure in examinations and quarrels with parents-in-law contributed a significant increase in the suicidal deaths during 1970 over 1969. The relevant statistics are furnished in Table IX. TABLE-1 Comparative Statement of Incidence of Suicides in States/Union Territories and Cities' 1969 / 1970
